passages.note: House Third Reading roll call on HB2853, the ESA expansion bill; Mathis is recorded voting No.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Enacted bill text showing HB2853 expanded ESA eligibility to effectively any public-school-eligible resident, the provision Mathis voted No on.

rows.reasoning: Mathis voted N on HB2853 (2022), whose operative section extends Arizona empowerment scholarship account eligibility to any resident 'eligible to enroll in a public school in this state' at preschool-for-disabilities, kindergarten, or grades one through twelve -- the bill's universal-eligibility expansion. Per the school-vouchers annex, a No vote on an expansion bill alone is direction-only and does not separate rung 1 ('Eliminating voucher programs') from rung 2 ('Opposing voucher programs and blocking their expansion, without moving to eliminate existing ones'), since the record shows no evidence either for or against repealing the pre-existing, narrower ESA program.
needs_source: Mathis's own words or a floor statement explaining the No vote on HB2853, to show whether he favors repealing the existing ESA program (rung 1) or only opposes further expansion (rung 2)
